title: USS Theodore Roosevelt Relieves George Washington in Middle East, Air Force Awards $16B Propulsion Contract, and Senate Probes Ukraine Starshield Access
subhead: The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS George Washington as Iranian attacks hit Bahrain and Houthi missiles targeted Saudi Arabia, while the US Air Force issued a $16 billion propulsion contract to 58 firms and US senators moved to investigate Ukraine's Starshield satellite access.

sections.heading: USS Theodore Roosevelt Arrives in Middle East as Gulf Missile Defense Intensifies
sections.body:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier strike group has arrived in the Middle East to relieve the USS George Washington, sustaining continuous US carrier presence in the theater, The War Zone reports. The handover comes alongside heightened Gulf hostilities after Bahrain reported Iranian strikes hit a civilian industrial facility—while Tehran claimed it struck US positions—and the Saudi-led coalition intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles targeting western Saudi Arabia, Times of Israel and Anadolu Agency report.

Amid the regional surge, Qatari Defense Minister Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani held talks in Doha with CENTCOM chief Brad Cooper, while Israeli intelligence officials pressed Washington for renewed strikes on Iran during a US visit, Anadolu Agency and The Wall Street Journal report.
sections.whyItMatters: Maintaining overlapping carrier strike groups in CENTCOM underscores Washington's determination to deter further Iranian and Houthi escalation without committing to immediate offensive air campaigns.

sections.heading: US Air Force Awards $16B Propulsion Deal; Senate Probes Ukraine Starshield Access
sections.body:
The US Air Force awarded a massive $16 billion indefinite-delivery contract split among 58 companies for 'advanced propulsion enterprise work' extending through 2041, Breaking Defense reports. Meanwhile, US senators are preparing to investigate changes to Ukraine's access to SpaceX's Starshield military satellite network, with Senator Chris Coons questioning the consequences for US defense reliability, Breaking Defense notes.

On alliance ties, Canadian Defense Minister McGuinty said Ottawa has not yet seen operational changes despite Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's classified memo restricting Pentagon socialization with Canadian counterparts, as Canada joined NATO's innovation fund, Breaking Defense, Defense One, and The Hill report.
sections.whyItMatters: A 15-year propulsion enterprise award locks in long-term engine industrial capacity, even as congressional scrutiny over Starshield and Canada defense restrictions highlights policy friction inside Washington.

sections.heading: Auterion and Ukraine's Skyfall Form German Drone Venture; Sweden Launches K200 Interceptor
sections.body:
Autonomy software firm Auterion is launching a joint venture named Skyfall X Auterion with Ukrainian drone maker Skyfall to manufacture drones inside Germany 'outside the range of air strikes,' Breaking Defense reports. Separately, Sweden's Nordic Air Defence unveiled the K200 drone interceptor—successor to the Kreuger 100XR—designed to counter jet-powered threats including Russia's Geran-3a, and is pushing toward testing in Ukraine.

On European deterrence, France and Sweden held their first joint nuclear-deterrence exercise with no live weapons, while Denmark's parliament unanimously ratified a defense pact expanding US military access in Greenland, Defense News reports.
sections.whyItMatters: Co-producing Ukrainian drone designs inside Germany insulates supply lines from Russian long-range strikes while European air-defense start-ups race to field jet-drone interceptors.

sections.heading: Turkey Outlines Mecca Pact Limits and Notes US Munitions Delay Lifted
sections.body:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan clarified that Ankara's role under the Mecca Defense Alliance centers on defending Saudi Arabia and confirmed no decision has been taken to deploy troops to Yemen, Anadolu Agency and TRT World report.

Speaking on US-Turkey defense relations, Fidan added that political will exists to resolve bilateral defense disputes, noting Washington lifted delays on ammunition purchases even as CAATSA sanctions and congressional lobbying continue to limit maneuvering room, Anadolu Agency reports. Separately, Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi faces conservative backlash over plans to rein in Tokyo's next five-year defense budget amid US spending pressure, SCMP notes.
sections.whyItMatters: Lifting US ammunition holds signals incremental improvement in Ankara-Washington defense trade, though CAATSA restrictions and Tokyo's budget debate show allied procurement remains constrained by domestic politics.

sections.heading: UNIFIL Hands Positions to Lebanese Army; Pentagon Deploys Regent Squire Drone
sections.body:
In southern Lebanon, UN peacekeeping mission UNIFIL began handing over positions to the Lebanese Armed Forces as its mandate winds down, with mission leadership urging continued monitoring of ceasefire violations and humanitarian access, Anadolu Agency and NPR report.

Across maritime and budget domains, The War Zone reports the Pentagon is sending the Regent Squire wing-in-ground-effect uncrewed vessel to patrol Middle East waters under CENTCOM, while Breaking Defense notes a CBO finding that the US Navy's shipbuilding plan would require an average $53.8 billion annually—a 41% hike over the past five years.
sections.whyItMatters: UNIFIL's handover tests whether the Lebanese army can hold southern border positions without renewed conflict, while autonomous sea-skimming drones expand CENTCOM's low-cost maritime patrol footprint.

bottomLine: The arrival of the USS Theodore Roosevelt in the Middle East and a $16 billion Air Force propulsion contract anchor US force posture and industrial base planning, while European co-production of Ukrainian drones in Germany and congressional probes into Starshield show allied logistics rapidly adapting to wartime demands.
sources: The War Zone, Times of Israel, Anadolu Agency, Wall Street Journal, Breaking Defense, Defense One, The Hill, Defense News, TRT World, SCMP, NPR
